newsitem.title: USA: U.N. panel holds firm on Iraq oil sales- diplomats.
newsitem.headline: U.N. panel holds firm on Iraq oil sales- diplomats.

text.p: Members of the United Nations sanctions committee on Iraq said Thursday that Baghdad would not receive permission to change deadlines for selling its $2 billion "oil-for-food" accord allotment.
The firm line by the committee means that Baghdad will be held to the accord's requirement to export around $1 billion by early September or forego part of the oil sales altogether.

"The resolution says up to $1 billion (in each 90 days of the accord) in exports. It is up to them to decide how much they want to export. They have put themselves in a disadvantageous position," said a senior Western diplomat.
Further, another senior Western diplomat said if a request by Iraq for flexibility came before the Security Council it would be denied.
"The Security Council would turn around and say: 'you put yourselves in this position,'" the diplomat said.
Diplomats threw cold water on speculation in the oil market that Iraq might be allowed some flexibility in order to ease oil sales which have been delayed since early June.

Iraq has been allowed to sell oil since June 8 under a second round of the "oil-for-food" accord, but has held up oil sales until its aid distribution plan was finalized, apparently as a protest at U.N. delays in approving aid imports during the first round.

Some flexibility was allowed during the initial 90 days of the first round, which ran from December 10 to March 9, but diplomats have said that Iraq will be allowed to carry over only about five percent of the $1 billion to be sold during the first 90 days of the second round, which ends September 5.

During talks between top Iraq and U.N. negotiators earlier this week in New York, the Iraqi side stated their belief that it needed only to sign contracts worth $1 billion of oil, and not actually lift the oil for export, U.N. sources said Thursday.

"Iraq believes it does not have to sell the oil immediately, and that liftings can be staggered. The (U.N.) legal affairs department has been consulted, but it is really up to the (sanctions committee)," the source said.
Meanwhile, the aid plan is under review by the U.N. Secretariat and is expected to be approved by the end of July, according to senior U.N. Department of Humanitarian Aid (DHA) officials.
A new pricing formula and oil sales contracts must then be approved, a process that should be speedy if Iraq rolls over terms and contracts which applied in the first round.

Oil industry participants figure that Baghdad would need to export from 1.5 to two million barrels per day (bpd) in order to sell the $1 billion before the September 5 deadline. Exports averaged a little over 660,000 bpd in the first round.
